items.title: OpenAI CFO questions Altman's push for late 2026 IPO

featured_image.name: OpenAI hires former Nextdoor CEO Sarah Friar as first CFO ...

items.description:
A rift has emerged at the top of OpenAI over the timing and affordability of what could become one of the largest public listings in technology history. Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar has privately questioned CEO Sam Altman's push to take the company public as early as the fourth quarter of 2026, warning that OpenAI may not be organizationally prepared for such a move, according to a report by The Information published Saturday.[1]

Friar has also raised concerns about Altman's commitment to spend $600 billion on computing infrastructure over the next five years, citing doubts about whether the company's revenue trajectory can support purchases of that magnitude. The tensions between the two most senior figures overseeing OpenAI's finances and strategy represent an unusual public signal of internal friction at the world's most valuable startup.[2][3]

items.title: Chinese scientist reveals military uses for space solar project

featured_image.name: China looks set to build space solar power station-Xinhua

items.description: A senior Chinese scientist behind Beijing's ambitious space-based solar power program has published a paper outlining how the technology could be adapted for military operations, including surveillance, electronic warfare, and communications control, offering a rare public acknowledgment of the dual-use potential of one of China's most prominent energy megaprojects.

items.title: Study of 1,700 languages finds shared grammar rules

featured_image.name: Study of 1,700 languages reveals surprising hidden patterns | ScienceDaily

items.description: Despite the staggering diversity of the world's languages, many follow the same grammatical playbook. A large-scale study analyzing more than 1,700 languages has found that roughly one-third of long-proposed "linguistic universals" hold up under rigorous statistical testing, pointing to deep cognitive and communicative forces that shape how humans build language.[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew set to fly around the Moon on Monday
items.description:
Saudi Arabia has become the first Arab nation to participate in NASA's Artemis program after its domestically built Shams satellite was successfully deployed aboard the Space Launch System rocket as part of the Artemis II mission, the Saudi Space Agency confirmed over the weekend.[1][2]

The satellite, formally designated Space Weather CubeSat-1 in NASA documentation, is a 12U CubeSat that hitched a ride as a secondary payload when Artemis II lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on April 1. The Saudi Space Agency announced initial contact with the satellite on April 3, revealing its Arabic name — Shams, meaning "sun" — and outlining its scientific objectives.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran accuses IAEA of inaction over Bushehr strikes

featured_image.name: Why an attack on Bushehr nuclear plant would be catastrophic for ...

items.description:
A projectile strike hit near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday, killing a security guard and damaging an auxiliary building in what marked the fourth attack on the facility since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28, the International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed.[1][2]

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi expressed "deep concern" over the incident, stressing that "nuclear power plant sites or nearby areas must never be attacked" and warning that auxiliary buildings "may contain vital safety equipment". The agency reported no increase in radiation levels at the site.[2][1]

items.title: Artemis II crew flies past the moon in historic flyby

featured_image.name: Artemis II hits ‘two thirds’ mark on moon journey, shares new lunar photos: ‘History in the making’

items.description: As four astronauts sweep around the far side of the Moon on Monday, the historic Artemis II mission reaches its climax under the watch of two key figures on the ground: chief flight director Emily Nelson and mission manager Matthew Ramsey. The mission, which launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center, marks the first time humans have traveled to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC intelligence chief killed in US-Israeli strikes that left at least 34 dead

featured_image.name: Majid Khademi appointed new IRGC intel chief | Al Mayadeen ...

items.description: Coordinated airstrikes by the United States and Israel killed at least 34 people across Iran on Monday, the 38th day of the war, in attacks that struck Tehran, Qom, and the southern port city of Bandar-e Lengeh. Among the dead was Major General Seyed Majid Khademi, the head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' intelligence organization, according to an official IRGC statement carried by Iran's Fars news agency.[1][2]

items.title: Physicists cool nanorotor to quantum ground state in two dimensions

featured_image.name: Ground-state cooling of a nanoparticle along two directions ...

items.description: A team of European physicists has cooled the rotational motion of a levitated silica nanorotor to its quantum ground state in two dimensions for the first time, a result that opens new paths for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. The work, published in Nature Physics on April 6, represents a leap beyond previous experiments that managed the feat in only one rotational axis.[1][2]

items.title: Study: 84% of fire-vulnerable species face rising wildfire risk by 2100

featured_image.name: Experts reveal climate change drove extreme wildfire seasons across the  Americas, making burned areas much larger

items.description: Climate-driven wildfires will place nearly 84 percent of fire-vulnerable species at heightened risk by 2100, according to a study published in Nature Climate Change on April 5. The research, led by Xiaoye Yang of the University of Gothenburg, offers one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of how shifting wildfire regimes could reshape threats to global biodiversity.[1]
